tool.name: Analysis of artifacts with Tasmanian
tool.description: Quantify, visualize and summarize mismatches in deep sequencing data

param.name: @NAME@
param.label: @LABEL@
param.option: read is PCR or optical duplicate (0x400)

tool.command:
## tasmanian-mismatch requires a coordinate-sorted BAM with a .bai index next to it ln -f -s '$bam_input' input.bam && ln -f -s '$bam_input.metadata.bam_index' input.bam.bai &&
#if str($reference_source.reference_source_selector) == "history": ln -f -s '$reference_source.ref_file' reference.fa && #set $reference_fasta = "reference.fa" #else: #set $reference_fasta = str($reference_source.ref_file.fields.path) #end if
tasmanian-mismatch input.bam '$reference_fasta' --threads "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" --min-base-quality $basequality --min-map-quality $mapquality --position-mode '$position_mode' #if $bed_filename --bed-file '$bed_filename' --bed-filter-mode '$bed_filter_mode' #end if $normalize $plot --overlap-mode '$advanced.overlap_mode' $advanced.methylation_mode --min-fragment-length $advanced.min_fragment_length --max-fragment-length $advanced.max_fragment_length --region-size $advanced.region_size #if $advanced.required_flags -f ${sum([int($flag) for $flag in $advanced.required_flags])} #end if #if $advanced.filter_flags -F ${sum([int($flag) for $flag in $advanced.filter_flags])} #end if #if $advanced.excl_flags -G ${sum([int($flag) for $flag in $advanced.excl_flags])} #end if #if $advanced.discount_table --discount-table '$advanced.discount_table' #end if ## --plot derives the report name from --output-file, so write into the ## working directory and move the table afterwards (keeps tasmanian.html discoverable) --output-file tasmanian.tsv && mv tasmanian.tsv '$output_table'

param.name: bam_input
param.label: BAM alignment file
param.help: Coordinate-sorted BAM dataset. Galaxy provides the accompanying index automatically.

param.name: reference_source_selector
param.label: Reference genome
param.help: You can select a reference genome from your history or use a built-in index (Local cache)

param.name: ref_file
param.label: Select the reference genome from the list

param.name: ref_file
param.label: Use reference genome from history
param.help: You can first upload a FASTA sequence to the history

param.name: bed_filename
param.label: Select a bed file
param.help: Optional BED file with regions to mask or filter. It should contain at least 'chrN', 'start' and 'stop' and be tab separated.

param.label: How to apply the BED regions
param.help: Only used when a BED file is provided
param.option: mask - skip only the aligned bases that overlap the BED regions
filter - skip whole reads that overlap the BED regions

param.label: Position mode
param.help: Report mismatches by position along the fragment (insert) or along each read separately
param.option: read - read position, R1 and R2 reported separately

param.name: mapquality
param.label: Minimum mapping quality
param.help: Exclude reads with a lower mapping quality than this number. Default=10

param.name: basequality
param.label: Minimum base quality
param.help: Exclude bases with a lower base quality than this number. Default=20

param.label: Report normalized frequencies
param.help: Normalize counts within each (read number, position, reference base) group. The last column becomes 'normalized_frequency' instead of 'count'.

param.label: Produce the interactive HTML report
param.help: Renders the mismatch table as an interactive Bokeh plot

param.label: Read-pair overlap handling
param.help: How to treat positions covered by both mates of a pair
param.option: cut - split the overlap at its midpoint
stretch - rescale each mate over its half via a cubic spline, dropping no bases

param.label: Methylation mode
param.help: Treat C>T and G>A changes as C>C and G>G to avoid confounding by bisulfite conversion

param.label: Minimum fragment length
param.help: Minimum estimated fragment length required for a read to be counted. Default=25

param.label: Maximum fragment length
param.help: Maximum estimated fragment length allowed for a read to be counted. Default=10000

param.label: Discount table
param.help: Optional variant_discounts.tsv produced by tasmanian-diagnostics, used to subtract likely genomic variants from the mismatch counts

expand.name: required_flags
expand.label: Require these SAM flags (-f)
expand.help_text: Only reads that have all of the selected flags set are counted. Nothing selected means no requirement.

expand.name: filter_flags
expand.label: Skip reads with any of these SAM flags (-F)
expand.help_text: A read is skipped as soon as one of the selected flags is set.

expand.name: excl_flags
expand.label: Skip reads with all of these SAM flags (-G)
expand.help_text: A read is skipped only when every selected flag is set. Use this to drop one specific flag combination rather than each flag on its own.

param.label: Region size (bp) for indexed chunking
param.help: Size of the genomic chunks processed in parallel. Affects speed and memory only, not the results.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Tasmanian counts mismatches between aligned reads and the reference genome, broken down by mismatch class and by position along the read or fragment. Systematic artifacts introduced during DNA preservation, extraction, fragmentation or library preparation show up as position dependent mismatch signatures, which is how they can be told apart from true biological variation. A classic example is the C>T excess at read ends in FFPE material.
-----
**Inputs**
* A **coordinate-sorted BAM** dataset. The tool reads the alignment through its index, which Galaxy supplies automatically for the ``bam`` datatype. * A **reference FASTA**, either from a built-in index (local cache) or from your history. * Optionally a **BED file** of regions and an optional **discount table**.
-----
**Output**
A tabular dataset in long format with one row per mismatch class, read and position::
base_change read_num reference_order fragment_position count C>T 1 1 42 18 C>A 1 1 42 3 G>A 2 2 17 11
* ``base_change`` - the reference base and the observed read base, e.g. ``C>T`` * ``read_num`` - 1 or 2, which mate the count comes from * ``reference_order`` - which mate of the pair comes first in reference coordinates * ``fragment_position`` or ``read_position`` - depends on the selected position mode * ``count`` - number of observations, or ``normalized_frequency`` when *Report normalized frequencies* is enabled. Normalization is done within each ``(read_num, position, ref_base)`` group, e.g. ``C>T / (C>A + C>C + C>G + C>T)``.
When *Produce the interactive HTML report* is enabled, a second dataset holds an interactive plot of the same table.
-----
**Position mode**
* **insert** - positions are counted along the sequenced fragment, so a pair contributes a single coordinate system. Overlapping mate positions are resolved with the *Read-pair overlap handling* option. * **read** - positions are counted along each read separately and R1/R2 are reported apart. This is the mode to use when looking for read-position dependent artifacts.
-----
**BED regions**
* **mask** - only the aligned bases falling inside the BED intervals are skipped. * **filter** - any read overlapping a BED interval is discarded entirely.
.. class:: warningmark
This differs from Tasmanian 1.x, which reported per-region groups (inside, complement and outside the BED intervals) as separate column blocks of one wide table. Version 2 masks or filters instead, and the *boundary/confidence* option that went with the old grouping no longer exists upstream. The *softclips* option is also gone from this tool; the soft-clip identity threshold now lives only in the ``tasmanian-diagnostics`` binary.
-----
**Read filtering**
Three SAM flag filters are available under *Advanced options*. Each one takes a set of flag bits, which are added together and handed to the corresponding option of the tool:
* **Require these SAM flags (-f)** - a read is counted only if *all* of the selected flags are set. Selecting *first in pair* restricts the analysis to R1, for example. * **Skip reads with any of these SAM flags (-F)** - a read is dropped as soon as *one* of the selected flags is set. This is the usual way to exclude duplicates or unmapped reads. * **Skip reads with all of these SAM flags (-G)** - a read is dropped only when *every* selected flag is set, which targets one specific flag combination instead of each flag on its own.
*Region size* controls how the indexed BAM is split into chunks for parallel processing. It changes speed and memory use only, never the reported counts.
-----
**Discount table**
``tasmanian-diagnostics`` can emit a ``variant_discounts.tsv`` listing mismatches that look like genuine genomic variants rather than artifacts. Supplying it here subtracts those counts, which sharpens the artifact signal on samples with real variation.
